checks.title: hibernatemode is off
checks.cmd: pmset -g custom
checks.why: Hibernation (S4) writes RAM to disk and resumes from it. The Dortania guide avoids it by setting Misc > Boot > HibernateMode to None in config.plist; this pmset value is the macOS-side equivalent and is community advice, not a command from the guide.

fixes.why: Turns hibernation off for all power sources.

checks.title: standby is off
checks.cmd: pmset -g custom
checks.why: Standby is the delay between sleep and going into hibernation. The Dortania sleep guide turns it off.

checks.title: autopoweroff is off
checks.cmd: pmset -g custom
checks.why: Auto power off is a form of hibernation. The Dortania sleep guide turns it off.

checks.title: powernap is off
checks.cmd: pmset -g custom
checks.why: Power Nap periodically wakes the machine for network access and updates. The Dortania sleep guide turns it off.

checks.title: proximitywake is off
checks.cmd: pmset -g custom
checks.why: The machine wakes when your iPhone or Apple Watch comes near. The Dortania sleep guide turns it off.

fixes.why: Disables wake when an iPhone / Apple Watch is nearby.

checks.title: tcpkeepalive is off
checks.cmd: pmset -g custom
checks.why: The TCP keep-alive mechanism wakes the machine about every 2 hours. The Dortania sleep guide turns it off.

checks.title: No sleep or wake failures in the last 7 days
checks.cmd: since=$(date -v-7d +%Y-%m-%d); n=$(pmset -g log 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); f=$(pmset -g log 2>/dev/null | awk -v s="$since" '$1>=s' | grep -ciE '(sleep|wake) failure'); echo "lines=$n failures=$f"
checks.why: macOS logged failed sleeps or wakes. Per the Dortania sleep guide these are most commonly caused by incorrectly managed devices, mainly PCIe-based ones. The guide's main offenders are USB controllers and devices, GPUs, Thunderbolt, NICs, NVMe drives and CPU power management.

fixes.cmd: pmset -g log | grep -iE '(sleep|wake) failure|wake reason' | tail -20
fixes.why: Read-only: shows the most recent failure and wake-reason lines so you can see what woke or blocked the Mac.

fixes.note: Apply the power settings above first. Then work through the guide's main offenders: USB (map your ports), GPUs (make sure yours is supported), Thunderbolt, NICs, NVMe (NVMeFix.kext) and CPU power management. Also disable Wake on LAN in the BIOS, and add keepsyms=1 and swd_panic=1 to boot-args so a sleep panic leaves a readable log. Details are on the guide page. On Intel 300-series (Z3xx) boards, a "BIOS Restarted in Safemode" message at shutdown or restart is an RTC problem: fix AWAC and use DisableRtcChecksum, or AppleRtcRam with rtc-blacklist (see the RTC section). That can only be seen at shutdown, not checked from macOS.

checks.title: Nothing is preventing sleep right now
checks.cmd: pmset -g assertions
checks.why: Something is holding the Mac awake right now, often playing audio or video, a download, or a USB device. This is only a problem if it persists when you are idle.

fixes.why: Read-only: lists the processes holding the assertion.

checks.title: NVMeFix is loaded for NVMe drives
checks.cmd: k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); m=$(echo "$k" | grep -ci nvmefix); n=$(ioreg -rc IONVMeController 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'class IONVMeController,'); echo "nvme=$n nvmefix=$m loaded=$l"
checks.why: An NVMe drive is using the generic driver. Per the Dortania sleep guide, Apple's power management only covers Apple-branded drives, so NVMeFix.kext is needed for proper NVMe power management (also keep the drive firmware up to date).

fixes.note: Add NVMeFix.kext (acidanthera/NVMeFix) to EFI/OC/Kexts and to Kernel > Add, after Lilu. EFI Builder adds it when your report lists an NVMe drive. Rebuild and retest sleep.

checks.title: TSC sync kext on server / HEDT CPUs (hint)
checks.cmd: b=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string 2>/dev/null); if echo "$b" | grep -qiE 'Xeon.R. (CPU E[57]-|W-|Gold|Silver|Platinum|Bronze)|i[3579]-[0-9]{4,5}XE? CPU'; then c=hedt; else c=other; fi; k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); n=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'CpuTscSync|TSCAdjustReset|VoodooTSCSync'); echo "cpu=$c tsc=$n loaded=$l"
checks.why: This is a hint, not a detected fault: the guide gives no way to measure it. Per the Dortania sleep guide, some firmware (mainly HEDT/Server boards and Asus laptops) does not write the TSC to all cores, which causes wake problems. This check only looks at server-class Xeons (E5/E7/W/Scalable) and X/XE Core CPUs; desktop Xeons (E3) and Asus laptops are not covered.

fixes.note: Only if you have wake problems. Per the guide: VoodooTSCSync for most HEDT hardware, TSCAdjustReset for Skylake-X/W/SP and Cascade Lake-X/W/SP (its Info.plist needs your thread count), CpuTscSync for troublesome laptops. Add only one, then rebuild.

checks.title: CPU name matches the physical CPU (needs a Hardware Sniffer report)
checks.cmd: norm(){ printf '%s' "$1" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | sed -E 's/\((r|tm)\)//g; s/@.*//; s/[0-9]+(st|nd|rd|th) gen//g; s/[0-9]+-core//g; s/(cpu|processor)//g; s/[^a-z0-9]+//g'; }; m=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string 2>/dev/null); a=$(norm "$m"); b=$(norm "$OCAT_REPORT_CPU"); if [ -z "$a" ]; then echo "mac=unreadable"; elif [ -z "$b" ]; then echo "report=empty"; elif [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then echo "name=same"; else echo "name=different report=[$OCAT_REPORT_CPU] mac=[$m]"; fi
checks.why: The CPU name macOS shows differs from the CPU in your Hardware Sniffer report. A CPU spoof, a wrong report, or a report taken from another machine would explain it; real hardware is the report. Compare the two names below.

fixes.note: Make sure the report is from this machine. If it is, check the CPU-related settings: Kernel > Emulate (CPUID spoof), ProvideCurrentCpuInfo and the CPU / SMBIOS choice, and the OpenCore config you built from it.

checks.title: CPU core count matches the report (needs a Hardware Sniffer report)
checks.cmd: p=$(sysctl -n hw.physicalcpu 2>/dev/null); l=$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu 2>/dev/null); r="$OCAT_REPORT_CORES"; case "$r" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "report=none";; *) if [ -z "$p" ] || [ -z "$l" ]; then echo "mac=unreadable"; elif [ "$r" = "$p" ] || [ "$r" = "$l" ]; then echo "cores=same"; elif [ "$r" -gt "$p" ] && [ "$r" -lt "$l" ] && sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string 2>/dev/null | grep -q Intel; then echo "cores=hybrid report=$r mac_physical=$p mac_logical=$l"; else echo "cores=different report=$r mac_physical=$p mac_logical=$l"; fi;; esac
checks.why: macOS sees a different number of cores than the report, and it is not the hybrid-Intel pattern (P-cores with hyper-threading plus E-cores, which is reported as no verdict). On AMD this usually means a wrong core-count kernel patch.

fixes.note: AMD: set the core-count (cpuid_cores_per_package) kernel patches to your physical core count. Intel hybrid CPUs: macOS cannot use E-cores, so a lower count is expected.

checks.title: CPU name is complete and its core count is consistent
checks.cmd: m=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string 2>/dev/null); p=$(sysctl -n hw.physicalcpu 2>/dev/null); n=$(printf '%s' "$m" | sed -nE 's/.*[^0-9]([0-9]+)-Core.*/\1/p'); if [ -z "$m" ]; then echo "name=empty"; elif [ -z "$n" ] || [ -z "$p" ]; then echo "name=ok nocount"; elif [ "$n" = "$p" ]; then echo "name=ok count=match"; else echo "name=ok count=different name_cores=$n mac_cores=$p"; fi
checks.why: macOS reports an empty CPU name, or a name that states a core count (for example AMD '16-Core') that differs from the cores macOS sees. With AMD vanilla patches this usually means the core-count patches are wrong.

fixes.note: AMD: set the core-count kernel patches to your physical core count. Check the CPU name in About This Mac > System Report.

checks.title: System Integrity Protection is enabled
checks.cmd: csrutil status
checks.why: SIP is off or customised. This is not a Dortania post-install requirement: it is fine to leave it off while you need patches that require it, but re-enabling it once everything works is recommended.

fixes.note: SIP can only be changed from Recovery (or the OpenCore picker's recovery entry): open Terminal there and run `csrutil enable`, then restart. Also review NVRAM csr-active-config.

checks.title: SMBIOS serial number (iServices)
checks.cmd: system_profiler SPHardwareDataType 2>&1 | grep -E 'Model Identifier|Serial Number'
checks.why: The serial is missing. iMessage / FaceTime / iCloud need a valid, unused serial.

fixes.note: Generate a serial with macserial for your SMBIOS model and put Serial / MLB / SmUUID / ROM into PlatformInfo. Verify the serial at checkcoverage.apple.com: it should say it cannot be found / is not valid, not that it belongs to a real Mac.

checks.title: A graphics card is detected
checks.cmd: s=$(system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(n>0){ gpus++; ig = vi || (!vo && bi); if(ig){ igc++; if(!me) igb++ } else { dg++; if(!me) dgb++; else if(amd) am++ } } n=0 } /Graphics\/Displays:/ { hdr=1 } /^    [^ ].*:[ \t]*$/ { flush(); n=1; bi=0; me=0; amd=0; vi=0; vo=0; next } n && /Bus:/ { if ($0 ~ /Built-In/) bi=1 } n && /Vendor:/ { if ($0 ~ /Intel|0x8086/) vi=1; else vo=1; if ($0 ~ /AMD|ATI|0x1002/) amd=1 } n && /Metal/ { if ($0 !~ /Unsupported/) me=1 } END{ flush(); printf "hdr=%d gpus=%d igpu=%d igpu_bad=%d dgpu=%d dgpu_bad=%d amd=%d", hdr, gpus, igc, igb, dg, dgb, am }'); echo "$s"
checks.why: macOS lists no graphics device. Without a working GPU driver the display runs unaccelerated.

fixes.note: Check that the GPU is supported by this macOS version (GPU Buyers Guide), that the iGPU is enabled in the BIOS if you rely on it, and that Lilu and WhateverGreen are loaded.

checks.title: Lilu and WhateverGreen are loaded
checks.cmd: s=$(system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(n>0){ gpus++; ig = vi || (!vo && bi); if(ig){ igc++; if(!me) igb++ } else { dg++; if(!me) dgb++; else if(amd) am++ } } n=0 } /Graphics\/Displays:/ { hdr=1 } /^    [^ ].*:[ \t]*$/ { flush(); n=1; bi=0; me=0; amd=0; vi=0; vo=0; next } n && /Bus:/ { if ($0 ~ /Built-In/) bi=1 } n && /Vendor:/ { if ($0 ~ /Intel|0x8086/) vi=1; else vo=1; if ($0 ~ /AMD|ATI|0x1002/) amd=1 } n && /Metal/ { if ($0 !~ /Unsupported/) me=1 } END{ flush(); printf "hdr=%d gpus=%d igpu=%d igpu_bad=%d dgpu=%d dgpu_bad=%d amd=%d", hdr, gpus, igc, igb, dg, dgb, am }'); k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); a=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'as\.vit9696\.Lilu|Lilu\.kext'); w=$(echo "$k" | grep -ci 'WhateverGreen'); f=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'IntelGraphicsFixup|NvidiaGraphicsFixup|Shiki'); echo "$s lilu=$a weg=$w legacy=$f loaded=$l"
checks.why: A GPU is present but Lilu or WhateverGreen is not loaded. The Dortania DRM / hardware acceleration page lists this as the first thing to verify when acceleration or decoding fails.

fixes.why: Read-only: shows whether both kexts are loaded (the command the guide uses).

fixes.note: If either is missing, add Lilu.kext first and WhateverGreen.kext after it in Kernel > Add, then rebuild.

checks.title: No legacy graphics kexts are installed
checks.cmd: s=$(system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(n>0){ gpus++; ig = vi || (!vo && bi); if(ig){ igc++; if(!me) igb++ } else { dg++; if(!me) dgb++; else if(amd) am++ } } n=0 } /Graphics\/Displays:/ { hdr=1 } /^    [^ ].*:[ \t]*$/ { flush(); n=1; bi=0; me=0; amd=0; vi=0; vo=0; next } n && /Bus:/ { if ($0 ~ /Built-In/) bi=1 } n && /Vendor:/ { if ($0 ~ /Intel|0x8086/) vi=1; else vo=1; if ($0 ~ /AMD|ATI|0x1002/) amd=1 } n && /Metal/ { if ($0 !~ /Unsupported/) me=1 } END{ flush(); printf "hdr=%d gpus=%d igpu=%d igpu_bad=%d dgpu=%d dgpu_bad=%d amd=%d", hdr, gpus, igc, igb, dg, dgb, am }'); k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); a=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'as\.vit9696\.Lilu|Lilu\.kext'); w=$(echo "$k" | grep -ci 'WhateverGreen'); f=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'IntelGraphicsFixup|NvidiaGraphicsFixup|Shiki'); echo "$s lilu=$a weg=$w legacy=$f loaded=$l"
checks.why: IntelGraphicsFixup, NvidiaGraphicsFixup or Shiki is loaded. The guide says these patches were absorbed into WhateverGreen and must not be present alongside it.

fixes.note: Remove IntelGraphicsFixup.kext, NvidiaGraphicsFixup.kext and Shiki.kext from EFI/OC/Kexts and Kernel > Add, then rebuild.

checks.title: iGPU has graphics acceleration (Metal)
checks.cmd: s=$(system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(n>0){ gpus++; ig = vi || (!vo && bi); if(ig){ igc++; if(!me) igb++ } else { dg++; if(!me) dgb++; else if(amd) am++ } } n=0 } /Graphics\/Displays:/ { hdr=1 } /^    [^ ].*:[ \t]*$/ { flush(); n=1; bi=0; me=0; amd=0; vi=0; vo=0; next } n && /Bus:/ { if ($0 ~ /Built-In/) bi=1 } n && /Vendor:/ { if ($0 ~ /Intel|0x8086/) vi=1; else vo=1; if ($0 ~ /AMD|ATI|0x1002/) amd=1 } n && /Metal/ { if ($0 !~ /Unsupported/) me=1 } END{ flush(); printf "hdr=%d gpus=%d igpu=%d igpu_bad=%d dgpu=%d dgpu_bad=%d amd=%d", hdr, gpus, igc, igb, dg, dgb, am }'); echo "$s"
checks.why: An integrated GPU is listed without Metal support, so it is not accelerated. The guide's checklist for this: the SMBIOS must match your hardware (no Mac mini SMBIOS on a desktop, since a Mac mini has mobile hardware), the iGPU must be enabled in the BIOS and have the right AAPL,ig-platform-id (and device-id if needed), avoid unnecessary ACPI renames, and Lilu and WhateverGreen must be loaded.

fixes.note: Work through the guide's list above. The WhateverGreen Intel HD FAQ covers the platform-id and device-id values for your CPU.

checks.title: Discrete GPU has graphics acceleration (Metal)
checks.cmd: s=$(system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(n>0){ gpus++; ig = vi || (!vo && bi); if(ig){ igc++; if(!me) igb++ } else { dg++; if(!me) dgb++; else if(amd) am++ } } n=0 } /Graphics\/Displays:/ { hdr=1 } /^    [^ ].*:[ \t]*$/ { flush(); n=1; bi=0; me=0; amd=0; vi=0; vo=0; next } n && /Bus:/ { if ($0 ~ /Built-In/) bi=1 } n && /Vendor:/ { if ($0 ~ /Intel|0x8086/) vi=1; else vo=1; if ($0 ~ /AMD|ATI|0x1002/) amd=1 } n && /Metal/ { if ($0 !~ /Unsupported/) me=1 } END{ flush(); printf "hdr=%d gpus=%d igpu=%d igpu_bad=%d dgpu=%d dgpu_bad=%d amd=%d", hdr, gpus, igc, igb, dg, dgb, am }'); echo "$s"
checks.why: A discrete GPU is listed without Metal support, so it is not accelerated. The guide's checklist: make sure the GPU is supported (GPU Buyers Guide), the SMBIOS matches your hardware, and Lilu and WhateverGreen are loaded with no legacy graphics kexts.

fixes.note: Check the GPU Buyers Guide for your card and macOS version, and see the GPU patching pages of the Dortania guide.

checks.title: An AMD discrete GPU is present (needed for hardware DRM)
checks.cmd: s=$(system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(n>0){ gpus++; ig = vi || (!vo && bi); if(ig){ igc++; if(!me) igb++ } else { dg++; if(!me) dgb++; else if(amd) am++ } } n=0 } /Graphics\/Displays:/ { hdr=1 } /^    [^ ].*:[ \t]*$/ { flush(); n=1; bi=0; me=0; amd=0; vi=0; vo=0; next } n && /Bus:/ { if ($0 ~ /Built-In/) bi=1 } n && /Vendor:/ { if ($0 ~ /Intel|0x8086/) vi=1; else vo=1; if ($0 ~ /AMD|ATI|0x1002/) amd=1 } n && /Metal/ { if ($0 !~ /Unsupported/) me=1 } END{ flush(); printf "hdr=%d gpus=%d igpu=%d igpu_bad=%d dgpu=%d dgpu_bad=%d amd=%d", hdr, gpus, igc, igb, dg, dgb, am }'); echo "$s"
checks.why: This is a limitation, not a fault. Per the Dortania DRM page, hardware DRM (FairPlay 2.x / 3.x, as used by Netflix and Prime Video in Safari) needs a supported AMD discrete GPU (Polaris or newer), and it is broken on iGPU-only systems. A pass here only means an accelerated AMD card exists, not that it is Polaris or newer. Browsers using software DRM, such as Firefox or Chrome / Edge, work either way.

fixes.note: Use Firefox or a Chromium browser for streaming, or add a supported AMD GPU. If you do have one, follow the guide's shikigva steps (inject it on one GPU only) and test with VDADecoderChecker.

checks.title: An audio output device is present
checks.cmd: system_profiler SPAudioDataType 2>&1
checks.why: No audio output device was found. AppleALC is probably missing or the layout-id does not match your codec.

fixes.note: Make sure AppleALC is in your EFI and set a layout-id for your codec (EFI Builder > Customize > Audio lists the options), or use the alcid= boot-arg. Rebuild and retest.

checks.title: Bluetooth controller is detected
checks.cmd: system_profiler SPBluetoothDataType 2>&1
checks.why: No Bluetooth controller was found. That is fine if the machine has none; otherwise the firmware / kexts (BlueToolFixup, BrcmPatchRAM) may be missing.

checks.title: A Wi-Fi interface is present
checks.cmd: networksetup -listallhardwareports 2>&1
checks.why: No Wi-Fi interface was found. That is fine if you have no Wi-Fi card; otherwise check the card is supported (itlwm / AirportItlwm, or a native Broadcom card).

checks.title: USB ports have a port map applied
checks.cmd: s=$(ioreg -c AppleUSBHostController -r -l -w0 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(inport){ ports++; per[ctl]++; if(!hasc) un++; if(b) { bt++; if(hasc && conn==255) bt255++ } } inport=0 } { i=index($0,"+-o") } /"ports" = \{/ { mapc++ } i==1 { flush(); ctl++; next } i>0 { if(inport && i<=pind) flush(); if($0 ~ /<class AppleUSB[0-9]*(XHCI|EHCI)Port,/){ inport=1; pind=i; hasc=0; conn=""; b=0 } next } inport && /"UsbConnector" = / { hasc=1; conn=$NF } inport && /"bDeviceClass" = 224/ { b=1 } END{ flush(); mx=0; for(c in per) if(per[c]>mx) mx=per[c]; printf "ports=%d unmapped=%d max=%d bt=%d bt255=%d map=%d", ports, un, mx, bt, bt255, mapc }'); k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); u=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'USBToolBox|UTBMap|USBMap|USBPorts'); j=$(echo "$k" | grep -ci 'USBInjectAll'); echo "$s kext=$u inject=$j loaded=$l"
checks.why: No USB port map was found: no map is injected into the USB controllers (no ports table) and no map kext (USBToolBox/UTBMap/USBMap) is loaded. Per the Dortania USB guide, an unmapped system is limited to 15 ports per controller, which causes missing ports and sleep/wake problems. (Port types alone are not enough: macOS also reads them from the board's ACPI.)

fixes.note: Map your ports with USBToolBox (or the manual method in the guide), add the generated map kext (UTBMap.kext, with USBToolBox.kext) to EFI/OC/Kexts and Kernel > Add, then rebuild.

checks.title: TRIM is enabled on SSDs
checks.cmd: system_profiler SPNVMeDataType SPSerialATADataType 2>&1
checks.why: A drive reports TRIM as off. Not covered by the Dortania guide; enabling TRIM on third-party SATA SSDs is common community advice and does not apply to hard disks.

fixes.why: Enables TRIM for non-Apple SSDs. macOS warns about it and restarts.

checks.title: USB ports are not stuck at the 15-port limit
checks.cmd: s=$(ioreg -c AppleUSBHostController -r -l -w0 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(inport){ ports++; per[ctl]++; if(!hasc) un++; if(b) { bt++; if(hasc && conn==255) bt255++ } } inport=0 } { i=index($0,"+-o") } /"ports" = \{/ { mapc++ } i==1 { flush(); ctl++; next } i>0 { if(inport && i<=pind) flush(); if($0 ~ /<class AppleUSB[0-9]*(XHCI|EHCI)Port,/){ inport=1; pind=i; hasc=0; conn=""; b=0 } next } inport && /"UsbConnector" = / { hasc=1; conn=$NF } inport && /"bDeviceClass" = 224/ { b=1 } END{ flush(); mx=0; for(c in per) if(per[c]>mx) mx=per[c]; printf "ports=%d unmapped=%d max=%d bt=%d bt255=%d map=%d", ports, un, mx, bt, bt255, mapc }'); k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); u=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'USBToolBox|UTBMap|USBMap|USBPorts'); j=$(echo "$k" | grep -ci 'USBInjectAll'); echo "$s kext=$u inject=$j loaded=$l"
checks.why: A controller exposes 15 or more ports and no port map is applied. macOS has a strict limit of 15 ports per controller, so extra ports may not work. The common stop-gap, XhciPortLimit, is a hack that can corrupt data and should be removed once a proper map is in place.

fixes.note: Finish the USB map so each controller has 15 or fewer ports, then set Kernel > Quirks > XhciPortLimit to false. See the USB mapping pages of the guide.

checks.title: USBInjectAll is not left in after mapping
checks.cmd: s=$(ioreg -c AppleUSBHostController -r -l -w0 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(inport){ ports++; per[ctl]++; if(!hasc) un++; if(b) { bt++; if(hasc && conn==255) bt255++ } } inport=0 } { i=index($0,"+-o") } /"ports" = \{/ { mapc++ } i==1 { flush(); ctl++; next } i>0 { if(inport && i<=pind) flush(); if($0 ~ /<class AppleUSB[0-9]*(XHCI|EHCI)Port,/){ inport=1; pind=i; hasc=0; conn=""; b=0 } next } inport && /"UsbConnector" = / { hasc=1; conn=$NF } inport && /"bDeviceClass" = 224/ { b=1 } END{ flush(); mx=0; for(c in per) if(per[c]>mx) mx=per[c]; printf "ports=%d unmapped=%d max=%d bt=%d bt255=%d map=%d", ports, un, mx, bt, bt255, mapc }'); k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); u=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'USBToolBox|UTBMap|USBMap|USBPorts'); j=$(echo "$k" | grep -ci 'USBInjectAll'); echo "$s kext=$u inject=$j loaded=$l"
checks.why: USBInjectAll.kext is loaded. The Dortania guide says to remove it after mapping because it breaks how Apple builds port maps, and it can break your final map.

fixes.note: Once your map works, remove USBInjectAll.kext from EFI/OC/Kexts and from Kernel > Add, and set XhciPortLimit to false. Keep it only while you are still building the map.

checks.title: Bluetooth is on an internal USB port
checks.cmd: s=$(ioreg -c AppleUSBHostController -r -l -w0 2>/dev/null | awk 'function flush(){ if(inport){ ports++; per[ctl]++; if(!hasc) un++; if(b) { bt++; if(hasc && conn==255) bt255++ } } inport=0 } { i=index($0,"+-o") } /"ports" = \{/ { mapc++ } i==1 { flush(); ctl++; next } i>0 { if(inport && i<=pind) flush(); if($0 ~ /<class AppleUSB[0-9]*(XHCI|EHCI)Port,/){ inport=1; pind=i; hasc=0; conn=""; b=0 } next } inport && /"UsbConnector" = / { hasc=1; conn=$NF } inport && /"bDeviceClass" = 224/ { b=1 } END{ flush(); mx=0; for(c in per) if(per[c]>mx) mx=per[c]; printf "ports=%d unmapped=%d max=%d bt=%d bt255=%d map=%d", ports, un, mx, bt, bt255, mapc }'); k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); u=$(echo "$k" | grep -ciE 'USBToolBox|UTBMap|USBMap|USBPorts'); j=$(echo "$k" | grep -ci 'USBInjectAll'); echo "$s kext=$u inject=$j loaded=$l"
checks.why: A Bluetooth (wireless controller) device is on a USB port that is not marked internal (UsbConnector 255). The guide notes that Bluetooth runs over USB internally, and mapping it as a normal port can break Handoff and other Continuity features. (Any USB wireless controller counts, not only Bluetooth.)

fixes.note: In your USB map, set the Bluetooth port's connector type to 255 (internal), then rebuild. Not a fault if your Bluetooth is not connected over USB.

checks.title: Apple CPU power management (X86PlatformPlugin) is loaded
checks.cmd: v=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.vendor 2>/dev/null); f=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.family 2>/dev/null); m=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.model 2>/dev/null); b=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string 2>/dev/null); c=$(ioreg -rc AppleACPICPU 2>/dev/null | grep -c '<class AppleACPICPU,'); p=$(ioreg -rc X86PlatformPlugin 2>/dev/null | grep -c '<class X86PlatformPlugin'); fr=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null | grep -ci 'CPUFriend'); if echo "$b" | grep -qi amd; then t=amd; elif [ "$v" = GenuineIntel ] && [ "$f" = 6 ]; then case "$m" in 42|45|58|62) t=sandy-ivy;; *) if [ "$m" -ge 60 ] 2>/dev/null; then t=xcpm; else t=old; fi;; esac; else t=other; fi; echo "cpu=$t model=$m plugin=$p cpus=$c friend=$fr"
checks.why: X86PlatformPlugin is not attached to the CPUs, so Apple's XCPM power management is not running (the Dortania guide's test for it). Without it the CPU may not idle or boost properly. A no-verdict result is normal on Sandy / Ivy Bridge and AMD, which XCPM does not support (see their own sections in the guide).

fixes.note: Per the guide: make sure SSDT-PLUG is present and enabled in config.plist and EFI/OC/ACPI, and set to your first CPU thread (not needed on macOS 12.3 and newer). Haswell-E / Broadwell-E need a CPUID spoof (Kernel > Emulate) since XCPM does not support them natively. Rebuild and retest.

checks.title: CPUFriend has X86PlatformPlugin to work with
checks.cmd: v=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.vendor 2>/dev/null); f=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.family 2>/dev/null); m=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.model 2>/dev/null); b=$(sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string 2>/dev/null); c=$(ioreg -rc AppleACPICPU 2>/dev/null | grep -c '<class AppleACPICPU,'); p=$(ioreg -rc X86PlatformPlugin 2>/dev/null | grep -c '<class X86PlatformPlugin'); fr=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null | grep -ci 'CPUFriend'); if echo "$b" | grep -qi amd; then t=amd; elif [ "$v" = GenuineIntel ] && [ "$f" = 6 ]; then case "$m" in 42|45|58|62) t=sandy-ivy;; *) if [ "$m" -ge 60 ] 2>/dev/null; then t=xcpm; else t=old; fi;; esac; else t=other; fi; echo "cpu=$t model=$m plugin=$p cpus=$c friend=$fr"
checks.why: CPUFriend is loaded but X86PlatformPlugin is not. The guide lists X86PlatformPlugin as a requirement for CPUFriend (so Sandy Bridge and AMD CPUs are not supported), so the kext does nothing here.

fixes.note: Fix XCPM first (see the check above), or remove CPUFriend and its data provider if your CPU does not support it.

checks.title: H.264 hardware decoding works
checks.cmd: osascript -l JavaScript -e 'ObjC.import("VideoToolbox"); var r="vt"; try { r+=" h264dec="+($.VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(0x61766331)?1:0)+" hevcdec="+($.VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(0x68766331)?1:0); } catch(e) { r+=" dec_error"; } try { var ref=Ref(); var s=$.VTCopyVideoEncoderList(null, ref); var n=0,h=0; if (s===0) { var a=ObjC.castRefToObject(ref[0]); n=a.count; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) { var d=a.objectAtIndex(i); var acc=d.objectForKey("IsHardwareAccelerated"); var ct=d.objectForKey("CodecType"); if (acc && ct && Number(acc.js)==1 && Number(ct.js)==0x61766331) h++; } } r+=" enc_status="+s+" enc_total="+n+" h264enc_hw="+h; } catch(e) { r+=" enc_error"; } r' 2>&1
checks.why: macOS reports no hardware H.264 decoder, so video decoding falls back to the CPU. This uses the VideoToolbox API; the guide tests the same thing with its VDADecoderChecker tool (a download), which you can also run. The guide's checklist: a supported GPU (GPU Buyers Guide), an SMBIOS that matches your hardware (no Mac mini SMBIOS on a desktop), the iGPU enabled in the BIOS with the right AAPL,ig-platform-id, no needless ACPI renames, Lilu and WhateverGreen loaded and no legacy graphics kexts.

fixes.note: Work through the list above; the GPU group of this window checks Lilu, WhateverGreen and legacy kexts for you.

checks.title: HEVC (H.265) hardware decoding works
checks.cmd: osascript -l JavaScript -e 'ObjC.import("VideoToolbox"); var r="vt"; try { r+=" h264dec="+($.VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(0x61766331)?1:0)+" hevcdec="+($.VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(0x68766331)?1:0); } catch(e) { r+=" dec_error"; } try { var ref=Ref(); var s=$.VTCopyVideoEncoderList(null, ref); var n=0,h=0; if (s===0) { var a=ObjC.castRefToObject(ref[0]); n=a.count; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) { var d=a.objectAtIndex(i); var acc=d.objectForKey("IsHardwareAccelerated"); var ct=d.objectForKey("CodecType"); if (acc && ct && Number(acc.js)==1 && Number(ct.js)==0x61766331) h++; } } r+=" enc_status="+s+" enc_total="+n+" h264enc_hw="+h; } catch(e) { r+=" enc_error"; } r' 2>&1
checks.why: macOS reports no hardware HEVC decoder. Many GPUs simply do not have one (for example older Intel iGPUs), so this is only a problem if your GPU is known to support HEVC.

fixes.note: If your GPU supports HEVC, follow the H.264 checklist above. Otherwise this is expected.

checks.title: H.264 hardware encoding is available
checks.cmd: osascript -l JavaScript -e 'ObjC.import("VideoToolbox"); var r="vt"; try { r+=" h264dec="+($.VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(0x61766331)?1:0)+" hevcdec="+($.VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(0x68766331)?1:0); } catch(e) { r+=" dec_error"; } try { var ref=Ref(); var s=$.VTCopyVideoEncoderList(null, ref); var n=0,h=0; if (s===0) { var a=ObjC.castRefToObject(ref[0]); n=a.count; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) { var d=a.objectAtIndex(i); var acc=d.objectForKey("IsHardwareAccelerated"); var ct=d.objectForKey("CodecType"); if (acc && ct && Number(acc.js)==1 && Number(ct.js)==0x61766331) h++; } } r+=" enc_status="+s+" enc_total="+n+" h264enc_hw="+h; } catch(e) { r+=" enc_error"; } r' 2>&1
checks.why: VideoToolbox lists no hardware-accelerated H.264 encoder (Quick Sync / VCE / NVENC). Apps such as video editors and screen recorders then encode on the CPU. Some GPUs do not expose an encoder on macOS, so this is informational.

fixes.note: Check the same GPU checklist as for decoding. If your GPU has no macOS-supported encoder, this is expected.

checks.title: A laptop keyboard / trackpad driver is loaded
checks.cmd: L=0; sysctl -n hw.model 2>/dev/null | grep -qi '^MacBook' && L=1; ioreg -rc AppleSmartBattery 2>/dev/null | grep -q '<class AppleSmartBattery' && L=1; k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); n=$(echo "$k" | awk '{print $6}' | grep -ciE 'ps2controller|voodooi2c$|voodoormi|voodoosmbus|AppleHSSPI|AppleUSBTopCase'); echo "laptop=$L driver=$n loaded=$l"
checks.why: This looks like a laptop but no input driver is loaded (VoodooPS2, VoodooI2C, VoodooRMI / SMBus, or Apple's SPI / top-case drivers), so the built-in keyboard and trackpad may not work. Ignore this if your laptop's keyboard and trackpad are USB devices. Laptop detection uses the SMBIOS model or a battery, so it cannot tell on a desktop.

fixes.note: Add VoodooPS2Controller (PS/2 keyboard and most trackpads) and/or VoodooI2C with its satellite kext (I2C trackpads), plus VoodooInput, then rebuild.

checks.title: VoodooInput loads before VoodooPS2 / VoodooI2C
checks.cmd: k=$(kmutil showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null); l=$(echo "$k" | grep -c .); echo "$k" | awk -v l="$l" '{ n=tolower($6) } n ~ /voodooinput/ { if(vi==""||$1+0<vi) vi=$1+0 } n ~ /ps2controller/ { if(ps==""||$1+0<ps) ps=$1+0 } n ~ /voodooi2c$/ { if(ic==""||$1+0<ic) ic=$1+0 } END { o="none"; if (ps!=""||ic!="") { if (vi=="") o="missing"; else if ((ps!=""&&vi>ps)||(ic!=""&&vi>ic)) o="bad"; else o="ok" } printf "order=%s input=%s ps2=%s i2c=%s loaded=%s", o, (vi==""?"-":vi), (ps==""?"-":ps), (ic==""?"-":ic), l }'
checks.why: The guide's fix for "keyboard works but trackpad does not": VoodooInput must be listed before VoodooPS2 and VoodooI2C in config.plist. Here it is loaded after them, or not loaded at all. (For VoodooI2C the guide wants VoodooGPIO, VoodooInput and VoodooI2CServices in any order, then VoodooI2C, then satellite kexts.)

fixes.note: In Kernel > Add, move VoodooInput above VoodooPS2Controller and VoodooI2C, enable only one copy of VoodooInput, rebuild. For I2C also make sure SSDT-GPIO is in EFI/OC/ACPI and enabled.

checks.title: A trackpad is detected (laptops)
checks.cmd: L=0; sysctl -n hw.model 2>/dev/null | grep -qi '^MacBook' && L=1; ioreg -rc AppleSmartBattery 2>/dev/null | grep -q '<class AppleSmartBattery' && L=1; h=$(ioreg -c IOHIDDevice -r -l -d1 -w0 2>/dev/null | awk '/\+-o /{ if(d) fl(); d=1; pg=-1; pu=-1; pr=""; next } /"PrimaryUsagePage" = /{pg=$NF} /"PrimaryUsage" = /{pu=$NF} /"Product" = /{pr=tolower($0)} function fl(){ n++; if (pg==1&&pu==2) po++; if ((pg==13&&pu==5) || pr ~ /track ?pad|touch ?pad/) tp++ } END{ if(d) fl(); printf "hid=%d hidptr=%d trackpad=%d", n, po, tp }'); q=$(ioreg -c IOHIPointing -r 2>/dev/null | grep -c '<class '); echo "laptop=$L $h legacyptr=$q"
checks.why: This looks like a laptop but no pointing device of any kind is visible to macOS. For a Synaptics PS/2 trackpad the guide suggests SSDT-Enable_DynamicEWMode (adjusted to your trackpad's ACPI device name, as the guide describes) as the first thing to try. This check cannot tell a built-in trackpad from an external mouse, so a mouse hides the problem (no verdict).

fixes.note: Check the Keyboard-works-but-trackpad-doesnt item (VoodooInput order). For Synaptics PS/2 trackpads, try SSDT-Enable_DynamicEWMode from the VoodooPS2 repository, adjusted to your device's ACPI name.
